# Results — Study 593 (HFEA — UPRO/TMF 55/45)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test
(Hedgefundie's Excellent Adventure, Bogleheads 2019) — **a 55/45 mix of 3x stocks (UPRO) and
3x long Treasuries (TMF), quarterly rebalanced, compounds faster than SPY thanks to leveraged
diversification** — run on the real funds since 2009 and, before their launch, on a
per-leg daily-leverage synthesis validated against the real funds (the
[study-100 melting-ice](../../100-melting-ice) recipe; corr must clear 0.99, and does).
Offline & deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number.
As-of **2026-06-30** (the last complete calendar month; the partial current month is dropped).
Fingerprint `b276ef14f488`.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily auto-adjusted (total-return) closes: SPY, TLT, UPRO, TMF + ^IRX (13-week T-bill, the financing / risk-free leg) |
| Window | 2002-07-31 → 2026-06-30 (**23.9** years; 6,017 days, 288 complete months) — starts at TLT's inception |
| Legs | real UPRO/TMF returns from **2009-06-26** (4,278 days); before that, the calibrated daily-leverage synthesis (1,739 days) |
| Rule | 55% 3x-S&P / 45% 3x-20y+-Treasury, weights reset at the **last trading day of each quarter** (96 resets, avg **13.5%** of NAV traded per reset) |
| Execution / costs | no forecast signal — the rebalance calendar is known in advance; the reset trades at the quarter-end close and the new weights earn from the **next session** (the one documented lag); costs one-way × NAV traded, 2/5/10 bps sweep |
| Benchmarks | SPY buy-and-hold and a 60/40 SPY/TLT quarterly-rebalanced mix, same machinery; Sharpe races are **excess-vs-excess** (monthly, minus compounded ^IRX); all legs **total-return, gross** unless labeled net |

> **Survivorship note.** All series are single, still-listed index funds (no basket selection),
> so there is no panel survivorship. The honest bias to name instead is **strategy
> survivorship**: HFEA is the *one* leveraged recipe that became famous because its 2010s
> backtest looked spectacular — the tape below shows exactly how regime-dependent that was.

## Synthesis validation — the study-100 recipe, per leg

Daily constant-leverage identity `r_3x = 3·r_index − 2·r_bill − fee/252`, all-in fee (expense
ratio + swap-financing spread) **calibrated on the real-fund overlap** so terminal NAVs match,
then validated on daily returns:

| leg | all-in fee | daily-return corr | ann. tracking err | NAV ratio (syn/real) | overlap |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|---|
| UPRO (3x SPY) | 2.13%/yr | **0.9983** | 3.01% | 1.0002 | 2009-06-26 → 2026-06-30 (4,278 d) |
| TMF (3x TLT) | 2.19%/yr | **0.9967** | 3.64% | 0.9998 | 2009-04-17 → 2026-06-30 (4,327 d) |

Both legs clear the 0.99 bar, so the 2002–2009 extension is a faithful stand-in. A pessimistic
**3.0%/yr** all-in fee on the synthetic era barely moves the headline (gap +5.18%/yr, t = 1.25).

## The full-period race (2002-07 → 2026-06, gross)

| portfolio | CAGR | vol | max DD | Sharpe | $1 grows to |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **HFEA 55/45 (3x/3x, qtr-rebal)** | **+17.47%** | 29.6% | **−70.8%** | 0.64 | **×46.8** |
| SPY | +11.24% | 18.8% | −55.2% | **0.68** | ×12.7 |
| 60/40 SPY/TLT | +8.99% | 10.7% | −30.1% | **0.75** | ×7.8 |
| UPRO leg alone (3x SPY) | +16.98% | 56.4% | −95.6% | 0.55 | — |
| TMF leg alone (3x TLT) | −0.39% | 42.6% | −92.7% | 0.15 | — |

The *allocation* claim is visible in the legs: the 55/45 mix out-compounds **both** of its own
components (+17.47% vs +16.98% and −0.39%) with half the stock leg's volatility — rebalanced
diversification genuinely converts two decaying 3x funds into a faster-compounding pair. But
the **risk-adjusted** case never materialises: HFEA's excess-vs-excess Sharpe (0.64) is *below*
SPY's (0.68) and well below 60/40's (0.75).

## "Compounds faster" — the inference

HAC (Newey-West) *t* on the mean monthly **log**-return gap (a geometric claim races in logs):

| race | log-CAGR gap | HAC *t* | n |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| HFEA vs SPY | **+5.42%/yr** | **+1.31** | 288 |
| HFEA vs 60/40 | +7.45%/yr | +1.91 | 288 |

**The full-period gap cannot clear the t ≥ 2 bar** — 24 years of a ~30%-vol strategy is not
enough sample to certify a 5%/yr edge. The regime split (the split point is the claim's *own
mechanism* — the 2022 stock-bond correlation flip — an ex-ante, not return-snooped, marker):

| window | gap vs SPY | HAC *t* | HFEA CAGR (Sharpe) | SPY CAGR (Sharpe) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 2002-08 → 2021-12 (ρ < 0 era) | **+11.22%/yr** | **+2.98** | +24.28% (0.92) | +11.03% (0.72) |
| 2022-01 → 2026-06 (ρ > 0 era) | **−19.71%/yr** | −1.59 | −8.02% (−0.09) | +12.18% (0.55) |

Welch *t* of the regime **difference** = **+2.23** — the two eras are genuinely different, not
noise. Pre-2022 the claim was real on the tape (and vs 60/40: +11.97%/yr, HAC t = +3.39);
since the flip it has run at −19.7%/yr. Robustness: real-funds-only window (2009-06 →) gives
gap +6.61%/yr at t = 1.25 (Sharpe 0.81 vs SPY's 0.96).

## The 2022 autopsy — the correlation flip kills both legs at once

The thesis's engine is *negative* stock-bond correlation: the bond leg insures the stock leg.
In 2022 inflation flipped the sign and both 3x legs crashed together:

| 2022 calendar year | return |
|---|--:|
| UPRO leg | **−56.8%** |
| TMF leg | **−72.6%** |
| **HFEA 55/45** | **−64.2%** |
| SPY | −18.2% |
| 60/40 | −23.5% |
| TLT (1x) | −31.2% |

| monthly SPY/TLT correlation | value |
|---|--:|
| 2002 → 2021 | **−0.30** |
| 2022 | **+0.51** |
| 2024 → 2026 | +0.32 |
| full sample | −0.10 |

HFEA's drawdown: peak **2021-12-27** → trough **2023-10-27**, depth **−70.8%**, and at the
as-of it still sits **−32.2%** below that peak (SPY made new highs long ago). Contrast with
the regimes the recipe was built on: **2008** HFEA −27.0% vs SPY −36.8% (3x bonds +109.9%
that year), **2020** HFEA +66.5% vs SPY +18.3% — when ρ < 0 held, the insurance leg worked
exactly as advertised.

## Costs — negligible at quarterly cadence (that is not the problem)

One-way costs × NAV traded at each reset (avg 13.5% of NAV, 4 resets/yr → drag is bps, not %):

| one-way cost | net CAGR | gap vs SPY | HAC *t* | annualised drag |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 2 bps | +17.46% | +5.41%/yr | +1.31 | 1.1 bps/yr |
| 5 bps | +17.44% | +5.40%/yr | +1.30 | 2.7 bps/yr |
| 10 bps | +17.41% | +5.37%/yr | +1.30 | 5.4 bps/yr |

Both ETFs are liquid and retail-accessible; the funds' internal costs (ER + financing) are
already inside their NAVs (and inside the calibrated 2.1–2.2%/yr synthesis fee pre-launch).
Tradability does not die on costs — it dies on the **−71% drawdown, the sub-SPY Sharpe, and
the regime dependence of the insurance leg**.

## Synthetic control — the machinery proof (never cited as market evidence)

Plant or remove the diversification engine in a seeded two-asset world (40y, 3x legs at 1%/yr
fee, 55/45 quarterly, race vs the 1x stock; **20 seeds averaged** — single-seed baselines are
banned):

| world | mean gap | mean HAC *t* | share of seeds t ≥ 2 |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| **PLANTED** (ρ = −0.6, bond carry +6%) | +10.36%/yr | **+4.90** (sd 0.88) | **100%** |
| **NULL** (ρ = +0.6, zero carry — the 2022 world made permanent) | −3.09%/yr | −0.83 (sd 1.03) | **0%** |

The harness banks the planted leveraged-diversification edge and refuses to manufacture one in
the permanent-2022 world — the machinery is faithful.

## Verdict

- **Signal — MIXED.** The full-period "compounds faster than SPY" gap is **+5.42%/yr** but
  only **HAC t = 1.31** — the tape cannot certify it. The verdict genuinely splits on the
  claim's own mechanism: in the negative-correlation era (2002–2021) the gap was
  **+11.22%/yr at HAC t = 2.98** (real on the tape); since the 2022 correlation flip it is
  **−19.71%/yr**, and the regime difference itself is significant (Welch t = 2.23). *Real on
  the ρ < 0 regime · reversed since the flip.*
- **Tradability — FRAGILE.** Vehicles are liquid retail ETFs and quarterly rebalancing costs
  are negligible (≤ 5 bps/yr drag) — but the strategy is a levered regime bet: **−70.8%**
  max drawdown, still −32% under water 4.5 years later, excess-vs-excess Sharpe **0.64 vs
  SPY's 0.68** (and 60/40's 0.75), and the entire insurance mechanism rests on a stock-bond
  correlation that has been **positive since 2022**. Real vehicles, fragile thesis — not
  INVESTABLE, not (quite) a Mirage: even including the disaster, $1 → ×46.8 vs SPY's ×12.7.
- **"Did 2022 falsify the thesis or just bruise it?" — MIXED.** More than a bruise: 2022
  falsified the *insurance assumption as a law* — the correlation flipped (+0.51 in 2022,
  still +0.32 in 2024–26), both legs crashed together (−57%/−73%), and the risk-adjusted case
  is gone (post-2022 Sharpe −0.09 vs SPY's 0.55). Less than a full falsification: the raw
  compounding claim still stands on the full tape (×46.8 vs ×12.7, +5.4%/yr gap) *including*
  the crash. The honest reading: HFEA compounds faster **when and only when** the ρ < 0 +
  bond-carry regime holds — the thesis is a regime bet that 2022 exposed, not a law that
  2022 merely dented.
